Answer: C
Reason: The initial radiograph (Figure 2) demonstrates asymmetric bilateral upper lung zone opacities with a relatively clear lower zone and no obvious Kerley B lines or pleural effusions, while the follow-up (Figure 3) shows rapid resolution of these opacities. This pattern of transient, non-dependent pulmonary edema that resolves quickly is characteristic of neurogenic pulmonary edema.
